# 1 Maccabees Chapter 4 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 4

---

## Council Notes

**On the prayer before Lysias (vv.30-33):** The allusion in v.30 is to two separate events: David vs. Goliath (1 Sam. 17) and Jonathan's raid at Michmash (1 Sam. 14). The author deliberately invokes Saulide as well as Davidic precedents, showing the Maccabees as heirs to all Israel's warriors. "The mighty warrior" (*andrei ischuro*) refers to Goliath.

**On the Hanukkah institution (vv.52-59):** This is the founding narrative of Hanukkah. The key elements are: (1) the date — 25 Chislev; (2) the coincidence with the date of defilement; (3) the eight-day duration; (4) the formal decree establishing it as perpetual. The translation must be clear and solemn.

**On "steadfast love endures forever" (v.24):** This is the refrain of Psalm 136 (*ki le'olam hasdo* in Hebrew). The Greek is *hoti agathos, hoti eis ton aiona to eleos autou* — "for he is good, for his mercy/steadfast love is forever." All translators recognize this as deliberate liturgical citation. "Steadfast love" (*hesed* / *eleos*) is the established rendering.

**On uncut stones (v.47):** The requirement for uncut stones (*lithous holoklerous*) comes from Exodus 20:25 and Deuteronomy 27:5-6. All translators note this legal citation. No disagreement.

---

1. Gorgias took five thousand infantry and a thousand picked cavalry, and this detachment moved out by night
2. to fall upon the Judean camp and strike it suddenly, guided by men from the citadel.
3. But Judas learned of it and moved out himself with his warriors to strike the royal force at Emmaus,
4. while the main army was still away from the camp.
5. When Gorgias came into the camp of Judas by night, he found no one there; he went searching in the hills, for he said: "These men are fleeing from us."
6. At daybreak Judas appeared in the plain with three thousand men, though they lacked the armor and swords they needed.
7. They saw the Gentile camp — strong and fortified, cavalry ringing it all around, trained fighting men.
8. Judas said to his men: "Do not be afraid of their numbers, and do not dread their assault.
9. Remember how our ancestors were saved at the Red Sea when Pharaoh pursued them with his whole force.
10. Now let us cry out to Heaven — perhaps he will favor us and remember the covenant with our ancestors and crush this army before us today —
11. so that all the nations may know that there is one who redeems and saves Israel."
12. The foreigners looked up and saw them coming against them.
13. They came out of their camp for battle, and the men with Judas sounded the trumpet.
14. They clashed, and the Gentiles broke and fled into the plain.
15. All the rearguard fell by the sword. They were pursued to Gazara and to the plains of Idumea, Azotus, and Jamnia. About three thousand of them fell.
16. Then Judas and his army turned back from the pursuit.
17. He said to the people: "Do not be greedy for the plunder, for there is battle still ahead of us.
18. Gorgias and his force are in the hills nearby. Stand now against our enemies and fight them, and afterward take the plunder with confidence."
19. Even as Judas was still speaking, a detachment appeared in the hills coming down to reconnoiter.
20. They saw that their forces had been put to flight and that the camp was on fire; the rising smoke made plain what had happened.
21. When they perceived this, they were seized with great fear; and when they also saw the army of Judas in the plain, drawn up and ready for battle,
22. they all fled to Philistine territory.
23. Then Judas returned to plunder the camp, and they carried off large amounts of gold and silver, blue and purple cloth, and great riches.
24. On their return they sang a hymn and blessed Heaven — for he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever.
25. Israel won a great victory that day.
26. Those foreigners who had escaped came and reported to Lysias everything that had happened.
27. When he heard, he was dismayed and disheartened, because things had not gone in Israel as he had intended, and the outcome was not what the king had commanded.
28. The following year he assembled sixty thousand picked infantry and five thousand cavalry to make war against the Judeans.
29. They came to Idumea and encamped at Beth-zur, and Judas met them with ten thousand men.
30. When he saw that the army was strong, he prayed: "Blessed are you, O Savior of Israel, who broke the attack of the mighty warrior by the hand of your servant David, and delivered the camp of the foreigners into the hands of Jonathan son of Saul and his armor-bearer.
31. Hem in this army by the hand of your people Israel; let them be put to shame with all their forces and cavalry.
32. Fill them with dread, melt the confidence of their strength, let them quake at their destruction.
33. Cut them down with the sword of those who love you, and let all who know your name praise you with songs."
34. They joined battle, and about five thousand of Lysias's men fell before them.
35. When Lysias saw the rout of his forces and the boldness of Judas's troops — how ready they were to live or to die with honor — he withdrew to Antioch and began recruiting mercenaries, planning to return to Judah with even larger forces.
36. Then Judas and his brothers said: "Now that our enemies are crushed, let us go up to purify the sanctuary and rededicate it."
37. The whole army mustered and went up to Mount Zion.
38. They found the sanctuary desolate, the altar profaned, the gates burned down, weeds growing in the courts as in a forest or on some mountain slope, and the priests' chambers in ruins.
39. They tore their garments and made great lamentation, and sprinkled ashes on their heads,
40. and fell on their faces to the ground. They sounded the signal trumpets and cried out toward Heaven.
41. Then Judas detailed troops to engage the men in the citadel while he purified the sanctuary.
42. He chose priests who were blameless and devoted to the Torah;
43. they purified the sanctuary and removed the stones of the defilement to an unclean place.
44. They deliberated about what to do with the altar of burnt offerings that had been desecrated.
45. The right counsel came to them to tear it down, lest it remain a disgrace to them, since the Gentiles had defiled it; so they tore it down.
46. They stored the stones in a fitting place on the temple hill, to wait until a prophet should come and give a ruling about them.
47. Then they took uncut stones, as the Torah commands, and built a new altar on the model of the previous one.
48. They rebuilt the sanctuary, the interior of the house, and the courts.
49. They made new sacred vessels and brought the lampstand, the altar of incense, and the table into the temple.
50. They burned incense on the altar and lit the lamps on the lampstand, and light filled the temple.
51. They set the bread of the Presence on the table, hung up the curtains, and completed all the work they had undertaken.
52. Early on the morning of the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month — that is, the month of Chislev — in the one hundred and forty-eighth year,
53. they offered sacrifice in accordance with the Torah upon the new altar of burnt offerings they had built.
54. At the very time and on the very day that the Gentiles had profaned it, it was rededicated with songs, harps, lutes, and cymbals.
55. All the people fell on their faces, worshiped, and blessed Heaven who had granted them success.
56. For eight days they celebrated the dedication of the altar, joyfully offering burnt offerings, a sacrifice of well-being, and thanksgiving.
57. They decorated the front of the temple with golden crowns and small shields, restored the gates and the priests' chambers and fitted them with doors.
58. There was very great rejoicing among the people, and the disgrace the Gentiles had brought was removed.
59. Judas, his brothers, and the whole congregation of Israel decreed that the days of the rededication of the altar should be observed with joy and gladness every year for eight days, beginning on the twenty-fifth day of Chislev.
60. At that time they also built high walls and strong towers around Mount Zion, lest the Gentiles come and trample it down as they had done before.
61. He stationed a garrison there to hold it, and also fortified Beth-zur to guard it, so that the people might have a stronghold facing Idumea.
